title: Deterministic Verification and a Single-Repair Guardrail for LLM‑Generated Network Configurations: a Paired, Shared‑Candidate Study
abstract: We report a sealed, preregistered paired experiment that measured the marginal verifier-detected effect of interposing a deterministic validator plus at most one automated repair on the same LLM-generated configuration candidate. Under preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation reused for both episodes per intent) we generated one candidate per natural-language intent with gpt-5-mini for N = 250 intent pairs and evaluated two episodes per intent: baseline (accept candidate) and guarded (deterministic_netops_validator_v5; if failing, permit a single automated repair). Execution completed 500 episodes with model_calls_used = 251 (250 shared initial generations + 1 repair). Results: baseline verifier-pass 249/250 (99.6%), guarded verifier-pass 250/250 (100.0%); contingency n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = +0.4 percentage points, 95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp] (paired bootstrap percentile, 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729), exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. The single discordant pair was converted to pass by the single permitted repair. The preregistered sim‑to‑real/production-like confirmatory contrast was not executed in this run; the reported confirmatory estimand and inference apply only to the synthetic/emulation partition that was executed. All run artifacts, preregistration, and analysis outputs are archived in the evidence bundle referenced in the Disclosure Statement.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are being explored as intent-to-configuration translators in network operations (NetOps) to accelerate device CLI authoring and intent-driven automation. Stochastic generation introduces operational risk: syntax errors, incorrect command ordering, local-policy violations, and vendor-CLI subtleties can produce unsafe or non-functional device changes. Prior empirical and survey work documents both the feasibility of LLMs to produce draft configurations and the need for deterministic verification or human oversight [1],[2].

A common architectural response is a generate–verify–repair (GVR) pattern: generated candidates are submitted to a deterministic validator and only validator-passed candidates are accepted or, if failing, subjected to bounded automated repair. Prior work shows GVR pipelines reduce mechanically verifiable error classes (syntax, simple ordering, local-policy violations), but the marginal benefit of such guardrails when modern LLM outputs are already well-formed under constrained tasks is not settled [3],[4].

This paper reports a sealed, preregistered paired experiment designed to isolate the marginal effect of deterministic validation plus a single allowed automated repair when the same initial model-generated candidate is reused across the baseline and guarded conditions (shared_initial_candidate semantics). The design intentionally holds generation constant across conditions so that only downstream deterministic validation and the single permitted repair can create a between-condition difference. Our confirmatory run executed N_pairs = 250 intents on a synthetic/emulation partition using the declared model gpt-5-mini and a deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). We quantify exact paired outcomes, compute inference via exact McNemar and paired-bootstrap CIs, and archive all execution and analysis artifacts for audit. The principal contribution is an artifact-grounded quantification of the marginal verifier-detected improvement (and its statistical bounds) under shared_initial_candidate semantics for a constrained NetOps task set.
sections.related_work:
Surveys and empirical studies establish the context for LLM-augmented NetOps and validator-assisted pipelines. Several studies demonstrate that LLMs can generate usable draft configurations in controlled or emulation settings, while also documenting remaining syntax/semantic errors that motivate verification layers [1],[2],[5]. Deterministic verification tools and formal-analysis techniques (e.g., Batfish, header-space and model-checking approaches) are mature methods for checking reachability, forwarding, and many local-policy properties and are used as validators in research and practice [3],[6].

Generate-and-verify architectures and program-repair workflows have been studied in code and configuration domains and are shown to increase detection and correction of mechanically checkable defects; limitations remain for deeper semantic correctness, vendor heterogeneity, and adversarial inputs [4],[7]. Prompt-injection threat analyses emphasize the need for filtering and validation layers in LLM-integrated pipelines but show adaptive adversaries remain an unresolved operational threat [8].

This study differs in three ways: (i) it uses a preregistered paired design with shared_initial_candidate semantics that isolates the validator/repair marginal effect on identical candidates; (ii) it provides comprehensive provider-call and stage-level reconciliation (shared initial generation versus repair stages) to reconcile model-call accounting; and (iii) it archives deterministic validator traces and analysis artifacts that permit exact numeric replication of the primary estimand and inference.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The experiment was preregistered as study-cand-2026-LLM-verifier-sim2real-v1 and defined a confirmatory paired binary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline with N_pairs = 250 and generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate. The preregistration froze the single-repair policy, inclusion/exclusion rules, contamination detectors, statistical tests (exact McNemar two-sided and paired-bootstrap percentile CIs), maximum model-call budget, and analysis plan. The preregistration artifact SHA-256 is recorded in the evidence bundle (reported succinctly in the Disclosure Statement).

Shared_initial_candidate semantics (implemented). For each intent a single initial model-generation call was produced and that identical candidate was evaluated under both episodes: baseline (accept candidate) and guarded (deterministic validation; if failing, permit up to one automated repair and re-validate). By design there was no independent per-condition first-pass generation; observed between-condition differences therefore arise only from deterministic validation and the single permitted repair.

Task generation and constraints. A deterministic task generator produced 250 constrained intents. Each task encoded initial and expected_final_state, allowed_touched_fields, required_sequence, and workflow constraints (e.g., make-before-break uplink switchover, paired-link atomic MTU changes). Difficulty labels (medium/hard/very_hard) were assigned deterministically to ensure coverage of common NetOps change patterns while limiting semantic ambiguity. The confirmatory run executed only the synthetic/emulation partition specified in the preregistration.

Model, pipeline, validator, and repair. The declared model for initial generations was gpt-5-mini. The guarded pipeline submitted the shared candidate to deterministic_netops_validator_v5 implementing full_intent_constraint_validation: parsing CLI sequences, checking required_sequence ordering, validating workflow policies (group-activity and make-before-break rules), and comparing the resulting final_state snapshot to the task's expected_final_state. When valid = false the pipeline permitted one automated, template-driven repair designed to fix syntactic and straightforward ordering defects (e.g., reorder commands to satisfy required_sequence, split combined commands). No multi-iteration repair or human escalation was allowed by design.

Inclusion, contamination, and missingness rules. The preregistered exclusions removed items that deterministically prevented verification (vendor-parser failures) or contained denylisted credential-like tokens; contamination detectors flagged instruction-like embedded tokens or private-address artifacts. Flagged items would be excluded from the primary analysis and handled in sensitivity analyses. In the executed confirmatory partition no episodes were excluded or flagged.

Statistical analysis. The primary analysis used an exact two-sided McNemar test on paired pass/fail outcomes and a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the guarded − baseline difference (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Preplanned sensitivity treatments included treating excluded or missing pairs as failures; none were required for the confirmatory set because complete_pair_count = 250.
sections.results:
Execution reconciliation. Execution completed the preregistered confirmatory partition: planned_episode_count = 500, completed_episode_count = 500, complete_pair_count = 250, and model_calls_used = 251. Provider-stage accounting reconciles to 250 shared initial-generation calls plus 1 repair call (stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 250, repair = 1); this per-stage distinction explains the observed hosted_model_call_event_count and aligns with the shared_initial_candidate semantics.

Primary binary outcomes and contingency. Deterministic validator-scored successes were: baseline_success_count = 249 (baseline_success_rate = 0.996) and guarded_success_count = 250 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0). The observed paired contingency was n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The single discordant pair (baseline failed, guarded passed) corresponds to the only exercised repair; repair-conversion on the confirmatory partition = 1/250 = 0.004 (0.4%).

Statistical inference. Exact McNemar two-sided test on discordant counts (n10 = 1, n01 = 0) returned p = 1.0. The paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the guarded − baseline paired difference (10,000 resamples; seed = 1729) is [0.0, 0.012], i.e., 0 – 1.2 percentage points. These numerical outputs and bootstrap parameters are recorded in the archived analysis artifacts.

Validator diagnostics and representative artifacts. Passed episodes show parsed_command_count and required_command_count equal to the task-required sequence length; for example, a hard-difficulty task with six required commands produced parsed_command_count = 6 and valid = true in both baseline and guarded episodes. Representative raw responses, normalized configurations, and full validator traces for sampled tasks (including the repaired pair) are archived and referenced in the evidence bundle for audit.

Missingness and contamination. No confirmatory episodes were excluded or flagged: complete_pairs = 250 and all missingness counts = 0. Contamination detectors flagged no episodes in the confirmatory partition, so no preregistered sensitivity adjustment was required for the primary estimand.
sections.discussion:
Operational interpretation. Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics and the constrained synthetic/emulation partition used here, the marginal verifier-detected benefit of inserting a deterministic validator plus a single automated repair was small: on these constrained tasks gpt-5-mini produced validator-conforming candidates in 249/250 cases and the guarded pipeline converted the single failing candidate via the single permitted repair. The paired-bootstrap CI upper bound (1.2 percentage points) provides an empirical bound on the possible verifier-improvement for this pipeline and task scope.

Why the marginal effect is small. Artifact-grounded factors explain the small observed gain: (1) the deterministic task generator encoded constrained intents and allowed_touched_fields that reduced ambiguity and favored well-formed CLI outputs; (2) the declared model produced highly consistent, syntactically well-formed sequences for these constrained intents; and (3) the deterministic validator checks only mechanically verifiable properties (syntax, ordering, final_state snapshot) and therefore does not detect broader runtime or emergent protocol issues that were outside the task specification.

Power and assumptions. The preregistration power calculation assumed a baseline pass rate ≈ 0.90 when selecting N_pairs = 250 to detect a 15-percentage-point absolute effect with ≈80% power. The realized baseline pass rate (0.996) was substantially higher than assumed; this reduces the power to detect small absolute improvements and makes the bootstrap CI a more informative practical bound on plausible verifier benefit under these conditions.

Threats to validity and scope. Internal validity: results depend on prompt templates, the single-repair policy, shared_initial_candidate semantics, and the validator encoding. Construct validity: the deterministic validator measures mechanically verifiable correctness but does not assert live protocol-level correctness or capture vendor-specific runtime divergences. External validity: the confirmatory evidence covers only the synthetic/emulation partition; preregistered community and production-like partitions were not executed. Security: adaptive prompt-injection, retrieval-based, or vendor-targeted adversaries were not exercised here and remain open threats.

Practical framing. These results do not imply validators or repair stages are unnecessary in broader operational contexts. Different validators (e.g., richer vendor or runtime models), multi-iteration repairs, human escalation, adversarial testing, or production heterogeneity could materially change the benefit calculus. Our findings quantify the verifier-detected marginal effect under a precise and auditable experimental contract and thus provide one bounded datapoint for risk assessment in similar constrained settings.
sections.conclusion: We executed a sealed, preregistered paired experiment under shared_initial_candidate semantics to measure the verifier-detected marginal benefit of deterministic validation plus one permitted automated repair on identical LLM-generated configuration candidates. In N = 250 constrained synthetic intent tasks, initial gpt-5-mini candidates passed the deterministic validator in 249/250 cases; the guarded pipeline converted the single failing candidate via the single permitted repair. Observed paired improvement = 0.4 percentage points (95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp]; p = 1.0). We explicitly disclose that the preregistered sim‑to‑real confirmatory contrast was not executed and that the executed confirmatory estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline on the synthetic/emulation partition only. Broader production, adversarial, multi-model, and multi-iteration repair evaluations remain necessary to establish generality. All execution manifests, raw responses, validator traces, repair traces, and analysis artifacts referenced in this paper are archived in the evidence bundle described in the Disclosure Statement.

disclosure_statement:
Human role and autonomy boundary: After an autonomy lock required by the CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track, the autonomous system performed literature search, study selection, preregistration freeze, prompt preservation, model calls, deterministic validation, permitted repair execution, analysis, drafting, peer-review, revision, and finalization without manual human editing of technical content. A human Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and performed pre-lock infrastructure development only; no human manually edited manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock.

Models, tools, and framework: declared model used for initial generation = gpt-5-mini (provider recorded as openai_responses); deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5; deterministic task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. The executed guarded pipeline permitted at most one automated repair per episode as specified in the preregistration. Execution reconciled to model_calls_used = 251 (250 shared initial-generation calls + 1 repair) consistent with shared_initial_candidate semantics.

Preregistration and immutable prompt reference: preregistration study id = study-cand-2026-LLM-verifier-sim2real-v1 (preregistration SHA-256 recorded in the evidence bundle). Immutable master prompt used to initiate the autonomous run: provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). The full execution and analysis artifact bundle (raw model responses, task manifest, validator traces, repair traces, deterministic reconciliation, analysis CSVs and logs) is archived; the bundle includes the manifests and hashes necessary for deterministic verification and audit and is referenced here as the official evidence bundle for this study. For compactness and to preserve archive-level machine-verifiability, per-file paths and full per-artifact hashes are provided in that archived bundle rather than repeated in this Disclosure Statement.
limitations: Confirmatory scope limited to the synthetic/emulation partition; preregistered community and production-like partitions were not executed and remain exploratory.

Deterministic validator assessed mechanically verifiable properties (syntax and prescribed workflow sequences) but did not measure broader semantic or behavioral correctness (protocol dynamics, emergent interactions).
Only a single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and one validator implementation were used; results do not establish multi-model or alternate-validator generality.
Only one automated repair attempt was permitted by design; multi-iteration repairs or human-in-the-loop escalation were not evaluated.
Adaptive adversarial and retrieval-based prompt-injection attacks and large-scale production heterogeneity were not exercised and remain open threats.

The realized baseline pass-rate (0.996) departed substantially from the preregistered power assumption (~0.90), reducing power to detect small absolute improvements; the paired-bootstrap CI therefore provides the most informative practical bound under the observed data.
